instances.claim: This tells me that the cent stopped being used in transactions because its metal came to be worth more than its face value.
instances.why: Line 2 states the melt-value discrepancy and line 3 states the cent's disappearance from pricing, with no connective between them, so the second reads as the consequence of the first; nothing in the draft offers any account of why nothing costs a cent, and the two facts are in fact independent (the metal premium is not what removed the one-cent price point). The lines also point opposite ways — one says the coin is worth more than a cent, the other that a cent buys nothing — which is what makes the bare adjacency do the explaining.
